sources.title: Minerals
sources.facts: Planning for mineral extraction, safeguarding, impacts, restoration, aftercare and managed aggregate supply.
sources.guard: Guidance does not prove a site contains workable reserves or has permission.

sources.title: NPPF: facilitating the sustainable use of minerals
sources.facts: Sets national policy for safeguarding mineral resources and maintaining supply.
sources.guard: National policy is not a site allocation or extraction consent.

sources.title: Minerals surveys
sources.facts: Collects aggregate minerals and annual minerals raised surveys used for policy monitoring.
sources.guard: Survey coverage does not prove current parcel-level reserves or ownership.

sources.title: Aggregate minerals survey for Great Britain, 2023
sources.facts: Reports regional and national sales, flows, consumption and permitted reserves of primary aggregates.
sources.guard: Reported reserves and flows are aggregated and not exact-site evidence.

sources.title: Aggregate minerals survey 2019 user guide
sources.facts: Defines survey sub-regions, reporting periods and interpretation of aggregate sales and reserves.
sources.guard: A user guide does not validate a specific quarry or planning application.

sources.title: National and regional guidelines for aggregates provision 2005 to 2020
sources.facts: Historical provision guidelines informed minerals planning and regional supply expectations.
sources.guard: Historical guidelines are archive continuity, not current supply or consent proof.

sources.title: Practice guide 65: registration of mines and minerals
sources.facts: Explains registration of mines and minerals under the Land Registration Act 2002.
sources.guard: Registration procedure does not establish title, extent or extraction rights for a candidate site.

sources.title: Guide to reclaiming mineral extraction and landfill sites to agriculture
sources.facts: Explains agricultural restoration, soil resources and afteruse considerations.
sources.guard: Restoration guidance does not prove restoration is feasible, approved or completed.
